cases.question: I'm putting together a periodic report on large payments made by a specific customer cohort, split by what the payment was for. Among payments over $4000 (strictly more than $4000) made from the accounts of male customers born between 1974 and 1976, I need two figures: how many were household payments, and how many were made for a purpose other than household payment. A few rules to keep in mind: born between 1974 and 1976 means the birth year is 1974, 1975 or 1976; a customer's accounts are the ones they hold a disposition on; payments are the individual transactions executed on the account, not standing payment orders; a payment counts as other-purpose only if it has a recorded purpose different from household payment, and a payment with no purpose recorded counts in neither bucket.
cases.evidence: SIPO stands for household payment.

cases.question: I want to find out whether our borrowing households from larger population centres transact differently from local ones. For every account at the Prachatice branch that has taken at least one loan, please give me: the account number, the account opening date, the total amount ever borrowed, how many outside bank counterparties the account has transacted with over its entire history, the owner's home district, the population of that district, and a rank of these borrowing households by home-district population from largest to smallest. Note that a counterparty means a particular bank account at another institution, identified by that account number, not by the bank code, and only transfers to or from another bank count — handling cash at our own branch does not involve a counterparty. A household's home district is the district its owner client is registered in, which is not necessarily Prachatice. For the ranking: largest population first, ties share the same rank and the next rank after a tie is skipped, and among households whose home districts have the same population, list the smaller account number first.
cases.evidence: An outside bank counterparty is a bank account at another institution that money was sent to or received from on a transfer transaction. District population is the number of inhabitants of the district.

cases.question: I'm profiling our gold-card customers for a regional campaign, split by gender. For women first, then men, look at gold-card holders whose card's account has an average balance over 1,000. Among the branch districts holding those accounts, keep only the districts with over 100,000 inhabitants. For each gender, tell me: the number of those districts; which of them has the most inhabitants, with its inhabitants figure - if two districts tie, list both, one row per district; the average salary across those districts, rounded to two decimals; and the average ratio of urban inhabitants across those districts, rounded to two decimals. Nothing else. Please note: 'over' means strictly greater than, and an account's average balance is the mean of its balances after each transaction.
cases.evidence: A gold card is a card of type 'gold', and its holder is the client linked to its account as type 'OWNER'. The district of an account is the district of the branch that holds it; a district's inhabitants, salary and urban-inhabitant ratio are the district's own figures.

cases.question: I'm reviewing what the money leaving our Pisek district branch's accounts is actually used for. What percentage of the total amount of outgoing payments that state a payment purpose went to household bill payments (SIPO)? Please give me a single percentage value, rounded to two decimals. Note this should be based only on payments that state a purpose, not all outgoing payments, and should consider the full transaction history.
cases.evidence: VYDAJ marks a transaction where money leaves the account. SIPO is the code for household bill payments. A payment states its purpose through its transaction characterization.

cases.question: I'm planning a regional campaign for female customers who hold a credit card and a loan, and I need a demographic profile per region. For each region, please give me: the region, the average district salary of the districts where these female clients live, and the average 1996 district unemployment rate of those same districts – both averages rounded to 2 decimal places. I also want the name of the most populous district among those districts in each region, so I know where to focus local advertising. A few rules: count only female clients who own the account (disposition type OWNER) and who have at least one credit card and at least one loan on that account. 'Most populous' means the district with the largest number of inhabitants; if two tie, take the one whose name comes first alphabetically. One row per region, and include every region that has at least one such client – nothing else.
cases.evidence: Disposition type OWNER means the client owns the account. Unemployment rate in 1996 is the district's unemployment rate for 1996; average salary is the district's average salary.

cases.question: I'm reviewing our presence in central Bohemia. Please tell me: the names of the three most populous districts of central Bohemia (largest by inhabitants), the number of crimes committed in 1996 in each of them, the average 1996 crime count across those three districts, the average 1996 crime count across all districts in the country, and the difference between the three-district average and the overall average (three-district average minus overall average). Rank districts by inhabitants, breaking ties by district name alphabetically (ignoring accents). Round all averages and the difference to 2 decimal places. The overall average should cover every district in the country, whether or not it has any accounts.
cases.evidence: Central Bohemia is the region of the Czech Republic surrounding Prague.

cases.question: For planning region-targeted card offers, I need to look at the smallest markets behind each credit card type. For each credit card type (gold, classic and junior), which home district of the clients holding that type has the fewest inhabitants, and how many inhabitants does that district have? Please include all three card types, and if several districts tie for the fewest inhabitants, list them all.
cases.evidence: By "home district" I mean the district a client lives in, and a district's inhabitants are its number of inhabitants.

cases.question:
I'm reviewing how our branches performed in 1996, and I'd like a picture of the money standing in accounts opened during that year, across the region that Litomerice belongs to (the region as given in the district table's region field).

For each district in that region where at least one account was opened in 1996 (openings counted by account creation date within the calendar year 1996), please give me:
- the district name,
- the number of accounts opened in 1996,
- the average end-of-1996 balance of those accounts,
with rows ordered by district name.

Also give me:
- the region-wide average end-of-1996 balance, taken across all those accounts (not as the mean of the district averages),
- the district with the highest average end-of-1996 balance; if two districts tie, name the one that comes first alphabetically.

By end-of-1996 balance I mean the balance after the account's last transaction dated on or before 1996-12-31; transactions dated 1997 or later don't count, and if several transactions fall on that last date, the one with the highest transaction id is the one that matters. Please round all averages to two decimals.
cases.evidence: Balance means the balance after a transaction.

cases.question: I want to check whether our biggest short-term loans cluster in populous branch districts and how well-off those areas are. Looking at 24-month loans on accounts with weekly statement issuance, take the ten largest loans ranked by approved amount from highest to lowest — if two loans have the same amount, the one with the smaller loan id ranks first, and ranking continues consecutively after a tie. The district of a loan is the district where the branch managing the loan account is located. Among the districts those ten loans come from, I need: the district with the most inhabitants (if two districts tie on inhabitants, the one with the smaller district id counts as more populous), that district's number of inhabitants, and the average salary across those districts rounded to two decimals.
cases.evidence: Weekly statement issuance means account issuance frequency 'POPLATEK TYDNE'. A district's inhabitants are its number of inhabitants, and its average salary is its average yearly salary.

cases.question: For every district with at least 100,000 inhabitants that has withdrawal transactions, can you show me the district name, region, population, total amount withdrawn in the district, withdrawals per inhabitant (rounded to 2 decimals), the district's rank by withdrawals per inhabitant (highest first), and the average standing-order debit per account held in the district (rounded to 2 decimals)? I want to compare withdrawal pressure and the standing-order burden side by side across our major districts. Please rank all qualifying districts, not just the top few, using competition ranking so tied districts share a rank and the next rank is skipped (e.g. 1, 1, 3). The whole transaction history on record is in scope. For the average standing-order debit per account, every account held in the district counts, including ones with no standing orders – those simply bring no debits.
cases.evidence: Withdrawal transactions are those recorded with type = 'VYDAJ'; a standing order is a recurring payment order that debits the account.

cases.question: I'm preparing a client review for client 3541. For each account this client can access, I need one row with: the account id, the date the account was opened, its frequency, the name and region of the district where the account is held, whether that district is the client's home district (Yes/No), that district's average salary, the loan repayment status (none if there's no loan), the loan amount (0 if no loan), the number of transactions over the account's whole recorded history, total income, total expense, net balance, the number of clients whose home district lies in that region, the name of the most populous district in that region, that district's number of inhabitants, and the account district's population rank within its region. Order the rows by number of transactions, most first, with ties broken by ascending account id. The client's home district is the district recorded for the client, and population means number of inhabitants. For ranks, the most populous district is rank 1; districts with equal population share a rank and the next rank skips.
cases.evidence: PRIJEM = incoming transaction; VYDAJ = outgoing transaction; net balance = total income - total expense

cases.question: I'm doing a lending review by account-opening year for my region. For accounts opened in the central Bohemia region from 1 January 1996 onward, broken down by the calendar year of the account creation date (as a text string like '1996', not an integer), I need: the number of accounts opened that year in the region, the total amount lent on those accounts, and the average across the districts of the amount lent per account opened in that district, rounded to two decimals. An account with no loan counts as having lent nothing.
cases.evidence: Central Bohemia is the region value recorded for districts in the region data; the amount lent on an account is the total of the loans granted on that account.

cases.question: For a regional risk review, I need to look at our largest 24-month loans. Please find the ten loans with the largest approved amount among loans with a 24-month duration on accounts that have weekly statement issuance. For each of these ten loans, give me: the district of the branch servicing the account, the approved amount, the approval date, and the account balance at the end of the day the loan was approved. Two rules: if two loans have the same approved amount, the one approved earlier counts as larger; and if several transactions share that last day, the one with the higher transaction id counts as the later one. List the results from the largest approved amount down.
cases.evidence: Weekly statement issuance means statement frequency is 'POPLATEK TYDNE'; loan duration is stated in months.

cases.question: The loan of 98832 approved on January 3rd, 1996 has one applicant account. For that account, list every counterparty it had paid before January 3rd, 1996. A counterparty means a specific account number at a specific bank, so give me one row per bank code and account number combination. For each counterparty I need the bank code, the account number, the number of outgoing payments made to them, and the total amount paid to them. Count only outgoing payments (VYDAJ, i.e. debits) made before January 3rd, 1996, and sort the counterparties by total amount paid, largest first.
cases.evidence: VYDAJ denotes an outgoing payment (debit); PRIJEM denotes an incoming payment (credit).

cases.question: For the year-end review of my branch at location 1: how many accounts that were on the branch's books as of 31 December 1995 hold an active loan contract? I want a single integer, nothing else. An account counts only if it belonged to the branch on that date, and only contracts that are still active by their repayment status count - statuses A and B are finished contracts and shouldn't be included.
cases.evidence: Loan status C means an active contract in good standing; loan status D means an active contract with the client in debt. Both are active contracts.

cases.question: I need to profile our three largest loans held by female clients. Please report for each of these loans: the client id, loan amount, duration in months, total payments, interest paid, loan status, the district and region of the branch where the loan's account is held, the account's transaction count and total deposits, an income category, the number of loans the bank has granted in that region, the average of the average salaries of that region's districts, and the client's completed age on 2026-10-09. A few notes: the three largest loans are the three highest approved loan amounts, and if amounts tie, include all tied loans. Total payments is the monthly payment times the duration, and interest paid is total payments minus the approved amount; round money figures to two decimals. The income category is High Income if total deposits exceed twice the loan amount, Medium Income if they exceed the loan amount, and Low Income otherwise. Loans in a region counts every loan the bank has granted in that region for all clients, not only female clients. The region's average salary is the average of the average salaries of the districts in that region, rounded to two decimals. For the age, use the completed age on 2026-10-09, subtracting one if the birthday hasn't occurred by that date.
cases.evidence: Female means client gender = 'F'. Deposits are transactions recorded as PRIJEM (credits to the account). District average salary is the district's average salary figure.

cases.question: I'm putting together a market-coverage report on how our 1997 rollout of monthly-statement accounts reached large urban districts. For districts with at least 100,000 inhabitants that had at least one monthly-statement account opened during calendar year 1997, please give me: the total number of monthly-statement accounts opened in those districts during 1997, how many districts are involved, and the average salary across these qualifying districts rounded to two decimals.
cases.evidence: Monthly statement issuance means the account's statement frequency is 'POPLATEK MESICNE'.

cases.question: I'd like to review the breadth of each gold-card account's external payment network. For every account that has a gold credit card, could you list: the account id, the district name and region of the branch, the total amount received, the total amount withdrawn, the number of loans taken, and the number of accounts at other banks that money was transferred to or received from? Then rank the accounts by that number of external counterparties. A few things to keep in mind: if accounts tie on the number, they share a rank and the next rank is not skipped; accounts with no external counterparty transfers should still be included and count as zero; and the totals and counts should cover the full recorded period.
cases.evidence: An external counterparty account is an account at another bank that money was transferred to or received from. Amount received refers to credit transactions, which carry transaction type PRIJEM. Amount withdrawn refers to debit transactions, which carry transaction type VYDAJ.

cases.question: I'm preparing our branch's annual customer review. For every account held at the Tabor branch as of 31 December 1996, I need a one-row profile per account, ordered among tied ranks by ascending account id, showing: the account id; the date the account was opened; the owner's gender and their age at 31 December 1996 in whole completed years; the number of credit cards issued to the account by 31 December 1996 (0 if none); the number of loans approved to the account by 31 December 1996 (0 if none); a loan standing label; the number of transactions on the account during 1997; the total money into the account during 1997; the total money out of the account during 1997; the peak balance reached on the account during 1997 (0 if none); and the account's rank by 1997 peak balance, highest first, with ties sharing a rank and the next rank skipped (e.g. 1, 1, 3). All 'as of' figures are taken at 31 December 1996; activity figures cover the calendar year 1997. A card or loan counts as held if it was issued or approved on or before 31 December 1996. The loan standing label is: 'no loan' if the account had no loans approved by 31 December 1996; otherwise 'defaulted' if any of its loans has repayment status B; otherwise 'repaying' if any has status C or D; otherwise 'paid off'. Money in is the sum of credit transaction amounts; money out is the sum of debit and cash-withdrawal transaction amounts. The account owner is the person with the 'OWNER' disposition on the account; other dispositions are just additional users. Nothing beyond these fields, please.
cases.evidence: Loan repayment status codes: A means the contract finished and was paid off, B means the loan was not repaid (default), C means the loan is running and being repaid, D means the loan is running and the client is in debt on it. Transaction types: a credit transaction brings money into the account, a debit transaction takes money out, and a cash withdrawal takes money out in cash.

cases.question: I'd like a district-by-district picture of where our classic-card-holding account owners send money outside the bank. For every district, give me: the district name, the number of clients who own an account and hold a classic credit card, the number of external accounts at other banks those clients paid through outgoing payments, and the total amount of those outgoing payments. A district means the district of the branch where the owned account is held — not the client's home district — and each client and every outgoing payment from the account they own counts toward that account's branch district. Include every district, even ones with no such clients or no such outgoing payments (show zeros). Use the whole recorded payment history. Order by total amount paid from highest to lowest, and alphabetically by district name when totals tie. Don't round the totals.
cases.evidence: An account owner is the client recorded as 'OWNER' on the account. An outgoing payment is a transaction recorded with type 'VYDAJ' (money paid out of the account). An external account is an account held at another bank to which the account holder sends money; the receiving bank together with the receiving account number identifies it.

cases.question: I'm planning services for our older female customers. For the clients who are female and were born before 1930, please look at the branches that hold their accounts, and then the districts those branches are located in. What is the average salary of those districts? Round the result to 2 decimal places. Note: born before 1930 means calendar birth dates before 1 January 1930.
cases.evidence: Average salary refers to the district attribute describing average salary.

cases.question: I'm preparing a campaign for senior female clients and want a sense of the economic profile of their home districts. Could you tell me the average of the average salaries of the districts where our female clients born before 1950 live? Please give me just that single figure, rounded to two decimal places.
cases.evidence: Average salary means the average yearly salary recorded for a district, in CZK.

cases.question: I want to know whether our small, healthy loans are concentrated in richer or poorer districts before we decide where to grow the small-loan business. Please give me one number: the average district salary, rounded to two decimals, across the districts where the accounts holding these loans are located. The cohort is loans with an approved amount below 100,000 that are still running without issues.
cases.evidence: Loan status C means the contract is running with no problems so far. District average salary is the average salary recorded for a district.

cases.question: I'm studying how client age relates to branch location. For each of two client cohorts, I want the cohort label and the average salary across the districts where the branches holding that cohort's accounts are located, rounded to the nearest whole number. A client's cohort is based on birth date: born 1980 or later is the young cohort, born 1919 or earlier is the old cohort. Note the district of an account is the district of its branch, not the client's home district. Give me one row per cohort, young cohort first. Nothing else.
By what percentage was Paul di Resta's fastest-lap speed in race 853 higher than in race 854? Use the speed in race 854 as the baseline and round to two decimals.
What percentage of Lewis Hamilton's recorded race entries from 2010 onward were not victories? Round to two decimals.
Which driver won the most recorded races? Give their first name, last name, nationality, and highest recorded driver-standings points total.

In the 1988 Australian Grand Prix, by what percentage was the winner's elapsed time shorter than the last full-distance finisher's? Use the last finisher's time as denominator and round to two decimals.
What percentage of Japanese-driver race entries from 2007 through 2009 matched their race winner's recorded lap count? Round to two decimals.
From 2000 through 2005, what percentage of race results were by drivers born before 1985 who completed more than 50 laps?
Which constructor scored most points from Monaco Grand Prix between 1980 and 2010? List the score, name and nationality of this team.
Who recorded the fastest Q3 qualifying time at Marina Bay Street Circuit in 2008? Give the driver's first and last name.
For each Formula 1 circuit in Italy with recorded laps, give the circuit name and its fastest recorded lap time in minutes:seconds.milliseconds format.

I'm comparing pit stop activity at the newer Grand Prix weekends. Among the 2017 races that were not hosted in 2000, what was the average number of pit stops per race? Please take the average of all of those races and round it to two decimal places.
cases.evidence: Hosted in 2000 means the race was on the 2000 race calendar.

cases.question: I'm writing a retrospective on German F1 drivers born between 1971 and 1985, and I'd like to quantify how often each of them reached the final part of qualifying. For every German driver born in 1971 through 1985 inclusive, over their entire career (every race on record), please give me their forename, surname, Wikipedia page link, date of birth, and the number of Q3 times they set. Sort the list from most Q3 times to fewest, and where two drivers have the same number, put the older one (by date of birth) first.
cases.evidence: Q3 is the third and final part of the qualifying session that sets the starting grid; a driver's Q3 time is the lap time recorded for them in that part.

cases.question: I'm writing a retrospective on the 1995 Japanese Grand Prix and want to highlight how far off the pace the slowest qualifier was. Could you tell me who set the slowest time in the first qualifying session (Q1) of that race? For that driver (or drivers, if two share the same slowest time, please list them all), I'd like their short reference name, nationality, birthday, and their Q1 time. To be clear, I mean the race named 'Japanese Grand Prix' in the 1995 season. Nothing else needed.
cases.evidence: By 'reference name' I mean the short driver code like 'hamilton'; by 'Q1' I mean the first of the three qualifying sessions; by 'birthday' I mean the driver's date of birth.

cases.question: For qualifying at the 1995 Japanese Grand Prix, I need the nationality of the driver who set the slowest time in Q1. If two drivers tie for the slowest Q1 time, give me each of their nationalities. I only want the nationality value(s), nothing else.

Who set the fastest time in Q1 at the 1995 Japanese Grand Prix, and what was that time? Please give me the driver's forename and surname, and the Q1 time. By '1995 Japanese Grand Prix' I mean the race of the 1995 season named 'Japanese Grand Prix'. If two drivers tied for the fastest Q1 time, list them all.
cases.evidence: Q1: the time a driver set in the first qualifying session.

cases.question: For the 2010 Formula 1 season, how many drivers did Lucas di Grassi qualify ahead of? I want a single number: the count of drivers he out-qualified over the whole season. By 'qualify ahead of' I mean recording a better qualifying position than that driver in the same race, with a lower position number being better. The 2010 season means the races held in the year 2010.
cases.evidence: qualifying position: the starting slot a driver earns in the qualifying session before a race

cases.question: I'm writing a recap of the 2017 Italian Grand Prix and want to credit the country of the quickest driver in the second qualifying session. Can you give me the nationality of the driver who set the fastest Q2 lap time in qualifying for the 2017 edition of the Italian Grand Prix? If two or more drivers tied for the fastest Q2 lap time, give me the nationality of each of them. I just need that nationality (or nationalities, in case of a tie), and nothing else.
cases.evidence: Q2: the second of the knockout qualifying sessions of a Grand Prix weekend.

cases.question: I'm writing an article about the Italian Grand Prix and want to know which first names recur among the drivers who finished second in that race. For every forename carried by two or more runners-up of the Italian Grand Prix across all its editions in the data, please give me one row with the forename and the number of runners-up who carried it. Order the rows from the most runners-up to the fewest, and alphabetically by forename when two forenames are tied. Leave out any forename held by only one runner-up.
cases.evidence: A runner-up is the driver who finished second in an edition of the Italian Grand Prix.

cases.question: For the 2017 Italian Grand Prix qualifying, what is the nationality of the driver with the second fastest Q2 time? Only drivers who took part in Q2 count, and by second fastest I mean the second smallest Q2 time. If several drivers share that time, list each of their nationalities.
cases.evidence: Q2 is the second qualifying session of a Grand Prix weekend, after Q1.

cases.question: For qualifying at the 2017 Italian Grand Prix, how many drivers set a time in the second qualifying session (Q2) faster than 1:40.000? I just need the count of drivers as a single number.

I'm reviewing the longest service pauses in races across the sport's whole history. Which racetrack saw the longest single pit stop ever? Please give me the racetrack name, location, country, the season year of that race, and the pit stop length. Consider all seasons in the data, and if several pit stops tie for the longest, give me one row for each of them.
cases.evidence: pit stop: a recorded pit-stop entry in a race; pit stop length: how long that pit stop lasted

cases.question: I'm researching the generation of drivers born in the 1980s and want to know how much final-session qualifying that generation actually did as a whole cohort. How many Q3 lap times did a driver born between 1981 and 1991 set on average? Count every driver born in that period in the average, including any who never set a Q3 lap time. Please give me the average rounded to two decimal places.
cases.evidence: Q3: the third and final qualifying session of a race weekend, whose times decide the top starting grid positions.

cases.question: I'm profiling drivers whose first name alone doesn't identify them. Across all races in the dataset throughout Formula 1 history, how many qualifying 1 times slower than two minutes were set by drivers who share their first name with at least one other driver and who have no code? I want just that single count.
cases.evidence: A driver's code is their three-letter abbreviation (e.g. 'HAM'); having no code means no such abbreviation is on record for them. The qualifying 1 time is the time a driver set in the first qualifying session of a race, one per race they took part in.

cases.question: I'm checking how much of the championship points for drivers named Robert came from races covered by the lap-by-lap timing archive. For every driver whose forename is Robert, I need their reference name and the total points they scored in races where lap-by-lap timing data exists for that driver in that race. The totals should cover all seasons and races on record.
cases.evidence: The reference name is the driver's short identifier, and points are championship points recorded for that driver's race result.

cases.question: For every edition of the French Grand Prix from the 1990 season through the most recent edition, I'd like to know which drivers set a fastest lap of the race slower than 90 seconds. For each such driver, give me the date of the edition, the driver's forename and surname, and their fastest lap time of that race in m:ss.mmm form. If several drivers in an edition clear that 90-second mark, list one row per driver. If an edition has no driver over 90 seconds, still show the edition with its date, but no driver or lap time. Please order the rows from the earliest edition date to the latest, and within an edition by driver surname alphabetically - if two drivers share the same fastest-lap time, order them by forename alphabetically.
cases.evidence: A driver's fastest lap in an edition means the shortest time they took to complete any single lap of that race, measured from the start of that lap; the 90-second threshold applies to that fastest lap, not to an average.

cases.question: I'm putting together a trivia fact about Italian drivers in Formula 1. Who holds the fastest lap time set in Q3 - the third and final part of qualifying - by an Italian driver, across the sport's entire history? Please give me the driver's forename, surname, and the fastest Q3 lap time exactly as it appears in the data. Only consider drivers who have a Q3 lap time recorded for some race, and if several Italian drivers share the exact same fastest Q3 time, list all of them.
cases.evidence: Q3 is the third and final part of qualifying.

cases.question: I'm writing a piece on the new generation of British Formula 1 talent. Among British F1 drivers born after 1980, who set the fastest Q3 qualifying time, what was that time, and at which race and in which year was it set? Please give me the driver's full name, the race name, the race year, and the Q3 time. By 'born after 1980' I mean the year of birth is later than 1980. If two qualifying results tie for the fastest Q3 time, I'd like a row for each.
cases.evidence: Q3 is the final part of the qualifying session that decides the front of the starting grid.

cases.question: We're writing a piece on F1's younger generation and want a number for it: how many drivers born in 1976 or later (born from 1 January 1976 onwards) have ever set the second-fastest lap of a race at any point in the history covered by the data? I just need the single count of such drivers.
cases.evidence: By second-fastest lap of a race I mean the driver's own fastest lap in that race was the second quickest among all drivers in that race.

cases.question: Who set the fastest time in Q3 (the final qualifying session) at the 2017 Italian Grand Prix? Please give me the driver's reference name (the short identifier like 'hamilton') as the result. If two drivers set the same fastest Q3 time, give me both of their reference names.
cases.evidence: Q3: the final qualifying session of a Grand Prix weekend

cases.question: Can you rank the Italian Formula 1 constructors by career points and give me the three highest-placed ones? For each, I'd like the constructor name, their career points, and their introduction website. Career points means the total of the points the constructor finished each season with (a season being one calendar year of racing). Constructors with no points still count, ranked with 0. If there are ties, they share a rank and the next rank is skipped (so 1, 1, 3), and I'd like every constructor within the top three ranks returned.

I'm working on a story about qualifying records. Across all races, which driver set the fastest time in Q3 (the final part of qualifying)? I'd like the nationality of that driver - and if more than one driver shares the fastest Q3 time, please give me every such driver's nationality. I don't need anything else, just the nationality or nationalities.
cases.evidence: Q3: the third and final part of the qualifying session.

cases.question: I'm putting together a historical note on constructor nationalities in Formula 1. For each constructor nationality, how many constructors from that nationality have recorded the fastest lap of a race? Please include every nationality in the result, with a count of 0 for nationalities where no constructor has done so. Count a constructor only when it is officially credited with the quickest single lap time in a race's recorded result - don't compute lap times yourself.
cases.evidence: Fastest lap: the constructor officially credited with the quickest single lap time in a race's recorded result.

cases.question: I'm studying how pit stop activity changed across the refuelling-rule change for Australia's F1 drivers. For each season from 2002 through 2013, can you give me the total number of pit stops made at the races of that season where, after the race, at least one Australian driver was placed better than 20th in the driver standings? I'd like the season year and the total pit stop count for each season. The pit stop total should cover every driver who pitted at those races, not just the Australian drivers.
cases.evidence: Better than 20th in the driver standings means a position of 1 through 19 after that race. A pit stop is any recorded pit stop made by any driver at the race.

cases.question: For the 1995 season (races held in the calendar year 1995), how many drivers set a Q1 lap time of more than two minutes - i.e., strictly longer than 2:00.000? I just need the number of drivers.
cases.evidence: Q1: the first of the qualifying sessions; a Q1 time is the lap time a driver set in that session.

cases.question: For my monthly recap I need the fastest pit stop made during any F1 race held in September 2016. Please tell me the driver's full name, the pit stop time, the name of the race where it happened, the circuit name, and the circuit location. If two or more pit stops share the fastest time, list each of them with its own driver, race, circuit name and circuit location.
cases.evidence: By pit stop time I mean the elapsed time of a pit stop, from the car arriving at its pit to rejoining the race.

cases.question: I'm profiling the oldest driver ever to win a Formula 1 race. Please identify the winning driver with the earliest date of birth - if two winning drivers share that birth date, use the one whose full name (forename then surname) comes first alphabetically. For that driver, return his full name (forename then surname), his nationality, the name and date of the first race he won (the earliest date; if two of his wins share that date, the one whose race name comes first alphabetically), and the total number of races he started over his entire career. A win means finishing in position 1 in a race. The career covers every race in the database, from 1950 through 2017. Return a single row.
cases.evidence: Grand Prix: any race event in the database, whatever its name is; some race names do not contain the words 'Grand Prix'.

cases.question: Across the history of the Canadian Grand Prix, how many runnings of the race have had at least one car retire with an accident? Please note that a crash in which the driver was killed is recorded as its own status and should not count as an accident here. I just need the single number of runnings, nothing else.
cases.evidence: accident: a car's race ends because of a crash

cases.question: For the 2017 Italian Grand Prix, which driver set the second-fastest time in the second qualifying session (Q2), and which constructor did he drive for that weekend? By second-fastest I mean the driver whose Q2 time comes next after the quickest one, counting every driver who took part in that session. If two drivers tie on Q2 time, the one who started the race higher up the grid counts as the faster of the two. Please give me the driver's forename, the driver's surname, and the constructor name.
cases.evidence: Q2: the second of the weekend's qualifying sessions; its times are measured to the thousandth of a second.

cases.question: I'm writing a season review piece and need the outright quickest Q2 time of the 2017 Formula One season – the fastest single Q2 time set at any race that year. Please give me the surname of the driver who set it and the name of the race where it was set. If two drivers share that fastest Q2 time, list every one of them along with the race names.
cases.evidence: Q2: the second of the three qualifying sessions of a Grand Prix weekend.

cases.question: I'm writing a race report and need to name the pole-sitter by their permanent race number. Who set the fastest Q3 qualifying time at the 2017 Italian Grand Prix (the race named 'Italian Grand Prix' in the 2017 season)? Please give me just that driver's permanent number. If two or more drivers share that fastest time, give me the numbers of all of them and nothing else.
cases.evidence: Q3 is the final part of qualifying, whose times decide the top starting positions; the fastest Q3 time earns pole position.

cases.question: For the 2017 Italian Grand Prix, who set the fastest lap time in Q3 (the final qualifying session), and what was that time? Give me the driver code along with the fastest Q3 time. If two or more drivers tie for the fastest Q3 time, list every tied driver.
cases.evidence: Q3: the third and final qualifying session; a driver's Q3 time is the lap time that driver set in that session

cases.question: I'm writing a report on the 2017 Italian Grand Prix (the one held in the 2017 season). Could you tell me the nationality of the driver who set the fastest time in Q3, the final part of qualifying? If several drivers share the same fastest Q3 time, please give each of their nationalities.
cases.evidence: Q3 is the third and final part of the qualifying session.

cases.question: Which Chinese Grand Prix edition from the 2000s (2000–2009 seasons) had the earliest scheduled local start time? Give me the season year of that edition and the runner-up's time gap to the winner (the runner-up being the driver classified second at the finish). If several editions share the earliest scheduled local start time, use the most recent one.
cases.evidence: Scheduled local start time: the time of day the race was scheduled to start, local to the circuit.

cases.question: I'm writing a qualifying report. Can you give me the driver codes of all drivers who set a time in the third qualifying session at the 2017 Italian Grand Prix? One row per driver who set such a time, and please list the codes in alphabetical order. Nothing else needed.
cases.evidence: The third qualifying session is the final segment of the race weekend's qualifying, in which only the fastest drivers take part.

cases.question: I'm writing about how the Canadian Grand Prix moved to early-evening starts. Could you find the editions of the Canadian Grand Prix from 2007 through 2017 (both years included) that began at 17:00 local time or earlier - a race that began exactly at 17:00 counts. For each one, give me the race year, the winner's forename, the winner's surname, and the winner's finish time. The winner is the single driver classified first at the finish. Nothing else, please.
cases.evidence: An edition is one running of the Canadian Grand Prix in a given year; local start time is the clock time of day, local to the circuit, at which the race began, on the 24-hour clock.

cases.question: I'm writing a retrospective on the 2017 Italian Grand Prix at Monza. For the Q3 session of that race's qualifying, can you give me the permanent career race number and surname of every driver whose Q3 lap time was strictly faster than 1 minute 38.000 seconds? I want all drivers under that mark, not just the fastest, and no particular order. Note that by permanent career race number I mean the number a driver carries throughout his career, not a one-off entry number for that weekend.
cases.evidence: Q3 is the third and final qualifying session; a driver only has a Q3 time if he actually took part in that session.

cases.question: I'm looking into fastest race laps recorded by drivers born in the 1980s. Can you tell me which three drivers born between 1980 and 1990 reached the highest single fastest-lap speed at any point in their career? I'd like their first and last names, ranked from the highest career-high speed down, and if two drivers are tied on that speed, list the one born earlier first, and then the one whose last name comes first alphabetically. Please give me just the three names, nothing else.
cases.evidence: Fastest lap speed: the average speed, in km/h, that a driver recorded on their single fastest lap of a race. A driver's career-high speed is based on that one lap, not an average across their laps.

cases.question: For the 2017 Italian Grand Prix, I need the list of drivers who were eliminated after the first qualifying session. Give me one row per eliminated driver with their reference name, ordered by their first-segment time from slowest to fastest. If two eliminated drivers have the same first-segment time, list the one with the lower driverId first.
cases.evidence: Eliminated after the first qualifying session means the driver took part in qualifying but did not go out in the second qualifying session.

cases.question: For my retrospective on the 1962 British Grand Prix – the race named 'British Grand Prix' in the 1962 season – how many drivers withdrew from that race? I just need a single whole number.
cases.evidence: A driver who withdrew from a race is recorded with the status 'Withdrew'.

cases.question: What was Elijah Allen's mean total expense per event for expenses dated in September or October? Round to two decimals.
What is the total amount spent on Student Club events in 2019 minus the total spent on events in 2020?
What note was recorded for the fundraising proceeds received on September 14, 2019?
What is the ratio of the Advertisement budget for the Yearly Kickoff meeting to that for the October Meeting?
Which closed events are tied for the highest ratio of total spending to total budget amount?
List the name of students that have attended more than 7 events.
Which members incurred at least one expense above the overall average expense cost? Give each member's first name, last name, and phone number as separate fields.

I'm putting together a review of last fall's activities and want to see how the Women's Soccer game compared to a typical event that semester. Please give me one row with: the number of students who attended the Women's Soccer event, the average number of students who attended events held in fall 2019 rounded to one decimal place, and a verdict of 'more', 'fewer' or 'equal' comparing the Women's Soccer head count to that average. Fall 2019 means events from 1 September 2019 through 30 November 2019 inclusive, and every event that semester counts toward the average even if nobody attended it. The verdict should compare the Women's Soccer head count to the rounded average: above it is 'more', below is 'fewer', exactly equal is 'equal'.
cases.evidence: Women's Soccer is an event name; attendance at an event is the number of members who attended it.

cases.question: I'm putting together our yearly report and need a breakdown of our 2019 events by event type. For each type of event we held in 2019, please give me: the event type, how many members attended that type's events during 2019, and the total amount budgeted for that type's events in dollars. A few notes: 2019 means the calendar year; the budgeted amount is the planned amount, not what was actually spent. If nothing was budgeted for a type's events, or no member attended them, just show zero. Please list one row per event type, in alphabetical order by event type.

I'm putting together a financial overview for the college that houses the Electrical and Computer Engineering Department. For each department of that college, can you tell me the total dues the club actually received from that department's enrolled members who took part in the club's events, in dollars? Please include every department of the college, showing zero if we received no such dues from it. Just the department name and the total dues per department.
cases.evidence: 'Dues' is the income source label for membership dues a member pays to the club; 'Member' is the club position of an enrolled member, as opposed to officer or inactive positions.

cases.question: For the mid-year budget review: I need to see, for each member who had to spend more than fifty dollars on an expense, how much room was still left in the budget lines those purchases were charged against. Please give me, per member, their first name, last name, and the total amount left across those budget lines in dollars rounded to two decimals. Order the results from the largest total down to the smallest; if two members have the same total, list them alphabetically by last name and then first name. The totals should cover all expenses on record, and if a budget line ended up overdrawn, its negative remaining amount should count toward the total.
cases.evidence: Spending more than fifty dollars on an expense means the expense's dollar cost is over 50. The amount left in a budget line is the amount budgeted for that line minus the amount spent against it.

cases.question: I'm putting together our year-end budget summary. How much did we collect in membership dues, in total dollars, from the students who attended the Football game? Membership dues are the payments recorded under the source 'Dues'.
cases.evidence: membership dues: payments recorded under the source 'Dues'

cases.question: How many majors offered by the college that offers Tyler Hewitt's major currently have no enrolled members in the club? Count every major that college offers, by major name.
cases.evidence: Enrolled members are the people recorded in the club's membership list.

cases.question: For our end-of-year report, I need one figure: the average number of members who attended each event that carried a budget line for advertising, covering every such event across the club's records regardless of when it took place. Please give it as a single number rounded to two decimal places.
cases.evidence: A budget line for advertising means a budget entry whose category is advertising.

cases.question: For every budget review event the club has held, can you give me the event name, its location, and the number of members who attended? I need this for the year-end report.
cases.evidence: 'Budget' is the club's event type for its budget review events, such as the Fall Budget Review and the Spring Budget Review.

cases.question: I'm planning study-partner pairings around our biggest social-attendance event. Can you tell me which academic majors were most represented among the members who attended the football game? For each major, give me the major name and the number of attendees in that major. If several majors tie for the highest attendee count, list all of them, ordered alphabetically by major name.
cases.evidence: Football game: the event named 'Football game'

cases.question: I want to gauge how much of the university's range of academic programs our club is failing to reach. Out of every major offered by the university - including majors where we have no members - what percentage have no club member studying them? Please give me just that single percentage, between 0 and 100, rounded to two decimal places.
cases.evidence: Major: an academic program offered by the university, as listed in the club's records of majors.

cases.question: Our officer team wants to settle a debate about whether we pull more weight than the rest of the club, so we need the attendance numbers before the next meeting. Could you tell us two things: the average number of events attended per officer, and the average number of events attended per other student, each rounded to two decimal places? To be clear on who counts where: officers are the members holding the position of President, Vice President, Secretary, or Treasurer, and everyone else in the club counts as an other student. Each average should cover every member of its group, and include every event in the club's records - there's no date cutoff.

I'm finalizing the semester wrap-up report and need one number: how many different kinds of things the club bought for events that went over budget this semester. A few things to keep in mind: an event counts as over budget if, in at least one of its budgeted categories, we spent more than we budgeted for that category - the budgeted amount minus what was actually spent came out below zero. Also, a single purchase can cover several kinds of things at once, and the purchase description lists what it bought, so make sure each kind is counted. The answer should cover the whole semester shown in the records, and I just need the single integer count, nothing else.
cases.evidence: went over budget: a budgeted category of the event ended with more spent than was budgeted for it, i.e. the amount budgeted minus the amount spent is below zero; kind of thing: a type of item bought, like water, pizza or posters

cases.question: For every event in our records that had at least one attendee, I need the amount spent per attendee on bottled drinking water, in dollars and cents rounded to two decimals. Give me one row per event with the event name and that amount; if an attended event had no water purchases, show 0.00, and if two events share a name, list them separately. Include all events regardless of status, across the club's entire history. A purchase that included water along with other items counts fully toward water.
cases.evidence: water: bottled drinking water bought for attendees

cases.question: For my report on the club's academic makeup, could you tell me how many members on the club roster major in a department of the College of Humanities and Social Sciences, and how many members do not? The two counts together should cover every member on the roster, with each member counted in exactly one of the two groups. A member counts as majoring in the college only if the department offering their major belongs to the College of Humanities and Social Sciences.
cases.evidence: The College of Humanities and Social Sciences is a college made up of certain departments; membership in the college is determined by which department offers a member's major.

cases.question: For our snack budget planning: among the events that spent money on chips, which event has the highest budget amount? By budget amount I mean a single budget line, not a total across lines - compare events by their largest single budgeted line. If several events tie on that largest line, list all of their names. Please just give me the event name(s).

I'm reviewing member engagement for our club's events in MU 215. Can you give me, for each event category of events held at MU 215, the number of club members who attended those events? Please count events regardless of their status (planning, open, or closed), and make sure every category that had events at MU 215 shows up, even if none of its events had any attendees.
cases.evidence: MU 215: the room name as the event location.

cases.question: I want to review what the money actually went on for the well-funded events, by venue. For events that had a budget line of more than forty dollars, how many different things were bought for them at each location? Please give me, for each location, the location of the event and the number of different things bought for such events at that location, and nothing else. Note that a budget line of more than forty dollars means a single budgeted amount strictly over 40 dollars, and all qualifying events held at a location should be pooled together.

I'm reconciling what we budgeted for September events against what we actually spent. Can you give me the total amount budgeted for the September 2019 events that served pizza? By September 2019 I mean events dated September 1 through September 30, 2019. An event counts as having served pizza if pizza was among the expenses booked to it. Please include every budget line for those events, whatever the category - not just the food lines. All I need back is the single dollar figure for that total.
cases.evidence: A pizza expense means an expense whose description is Pizza.

cases.question: Hi - I need one overall figure for the budget next year: what's the average total amount we've actually spent per event, counting all budget categories, across every event we've ever recorded? Please give me the average in dollars, rounded to two decimal places, with no date restriction.

Among our closed events that stayed within budget (total spending not exceeding total budget), which one had the most purchases? Please give me just that event's name. Consider every closed event that didn't go over budget, including events with no purchases at all. If two events tie for the most purchases, report only the one with the alphabetically first event ID.
cases.evidence: A purchase is a single item recorded on an expense record; one expense record may list several items. Total budget is the sum of budgeted amounts across all budget lines of the event; total spending is the sum of spent amounts across all budget lines of the event.

cases.question: For our year-end review, I want to know which event formats bring in the most people. Looking at our whole club year (every event from September 2019 through May 2020), which event type was attended by the most members, and how many members attended that type's events? If several event types tie for the most, list every one of them. Just give me the event type and the number of members for it - nothing else.
cases.evidence: By "attended" I mean a member coming to an event; event type is the kind of event, e.g. Meeting, Social, Game, Election, Community Service.

cases.question: I'm putting together next semester's purchasing plan and want to know which food and drink item the club buys most often. Among purchases made under the food budget only, which single item appears on the most purchase records, and how many purchase records mention it? If two items are tied, go with the one whose name comes first alphabetically. Please give me just the item's name and that record count.
cases.evidence: A purchase record is an entry in the club's expense records for money spent on a purchase.

cases.question: I'm wrapping up the October Meeting and need the final numbers broken down by what we actually bought, not just by budget category. For every item bought with approved money for the October Meeting, can you give me: the item's name, the budget category of the purchase that included the item, and the total cost in dollars of the approved October Meeting purchases that included the item? Only expenses marked as approved count - an expense without an approval mark doesn't. If an item was included in approved purchases recorded under more than one budget category, give me one row per category. Costs should be plain sums in US dollars with no rounding, and please sort the list by category and then by item name.
cases.evidence: An item is a single thing bought with club money, such as water, pizza or posters. A purchase is an expense recorded for the event.

cases.question: For our department report, I need to know how many different fields of study our club members from the Political Science Department represent. Only count members of the Political Science Department - members from other departments don't count. Just give me the number of different majors studied by those members.
cases.evidence: A major is a field of study offered by a department.

What is the average height, in centimetres, of Marvel Comics characters who have at least one power that no DC Comics character has? Only characters with a measured height count.

cases.question: For a segment on strength heroes, I want to know how many superpowers are held only by heroes who have Super Strength. cases.evidence: Super Strength is a super power name.

cases.question: I'm setting a typical weight for a green-skinned creature class. Can you tell me the average weight in kg of the heroes with green skin? Count only heroes whose weight is known, and give me one number rounded to one decimal place.
cases.evidence: Green skin means the hero's skin colour is green.

cases.question: I'm building a fact box on Marvel heroes' civilian identities. Among Marvel Comics superheroes whose full name (their civilian identity, like 'Richard Milhouse Jones') is known, which superpower is the most common, and how many of those heroes have it? If several superpowers tie for most common, list all of them with their counts. Just give me the superpower name(s) and the counts.
I want to profile the cohort of heroes whose Intelligence score matches Abomination's Intelligence score. What is their average measured weight in kg? Please round the average to two decimals.
cases.evidence: Intelligence is one of the six attribute scores a hero has (Intelligence, Strength, Speed, Durability, Power, Combat)

cases.question: I'm putting together a trivia page profiling blue-haired heroes by their abilities. For each gender, male and female, how many blue-haired superheroes have at least ten listed powers? I need the count for both groups, and by 'at least ten' I mean ten or more.
cases.evidence: Listed powers: the superpowers recorded for a hero.

cases.question: I'm putting together a comparison of the heaviest brick-strength characters. What is the average weight, in kilograms, of all superheroes whose Strength score equals the Hulk's? I just need a single integer rounded to the nearest kilogram. Include every superhero in the database, no restrictions on publisher or alignment. cases.evidence: Strength is one of the six measured hero attributes, each scored on a 1-100 scale; the Hulk is the superhero named 'Hulk'; weight is the superhero's weight in kilograms.

cases.question: For my 'giants of the genre' feature, I want to headline how varied the abilities of the tallest heroes are. How many different superpowers appear among the ten tallest superheroes? Rank heroes by height and take the top ten; if several heroes tie at the tenth-tallest height, include all of them. A hero counts among the ten tallest even if no powers are on file for them.
