cases.evidence: superpower = an ability such as Agility or Accelerated Healing, as named in the superpower list

cases.question: How many characters published by A-Bomb's publisher have no race listed? I just need a single count. (By A-Bomb's publisher, I mean the publisher that publishes the character A-Bomb.)
cases.evidence: race: the character's race or group, e.g. Human, Alien, Mutant

cases.question: For my cryokinesis page, I want to know how broad the power portfolios are around ice-powered heroes. Consider all heroes who share at least one superpower with a cryokinesis holder - including the cryokinesis holders themselves, since they share cryokinesis with each other. What is the average number of superpowers these heroes have, rounded to one decimal place? Please send back just that single number.
cases.evidence: Cryokinesis is the superpower to generate and control ice.

cases.question: I'm researching heroes like A-Bomb. What is the average height in centimetres of the superheroes in A-Bomb's group? Please give me just that single number, rounded to one decimal place. Note that A-Bomb itself belongs to its group and should be included, and only heroes whose height is actually on record should count toward the average-anyone without a recorded height should be left out rather than counted as some height.
cases.evidence: In this request, "group" refers to race.

cases.question: How many heroes published by Blackwulf's publisher have an eye colour that at least one hero from a different publisher also has? By "that publisher's heroes" I mean all of its heroes, not just Blackwulf. A different publisher means any other publisher, and heroes with no publisher listed shouldn't count as coming from a different publisher. I just want that single count back.
cases.evidence: Eye colour: the colour of a hero's eyes as catalogued for that hero.

cases.question: Which race is the most common among the superheroes published by the same publisher as the superhero whose full name is Charles Chandler? I'd like, for that publisher's superheroes only, the name of the most common race and the count of that publisher's superheroes of that race. Ignore any superhero with no race recorded. If several races tie for most common, list every tied race with its count.
cases.evidence: Race: the superhero's species or type, e.g. Human, Mutant, Alien.

cases.question: I'm writing a power-profile feature on heroes with super speed or death touch. Can you give me one number: the average intelligence score of the superheroes who have either of those powers? Round it to one decimal place, and only count the heroes who actually have an intelligence score in the database.
cases.evidence: "Super speed" and "death touch" are superpower names as used in the database; "intelligence" is the hero attribute by that name.

cases.question: I'm putting together a physical profile of the green-skinned villain corner of the universe for a fan wiki page. Could you tell me the average height in centimetres and the average weight in kilograms of the green-skinned villains? Please average only over the characters whose measurement is actually on record - a character with no recorded height or weight shouldn't drag the average down - and round each average to two decimals. I just need those two numbers.
cases.evidence: By 'villain' I mean a character whose alignment is Bad, and by 'green-skinned' I mean a character whose skin colour is Green. Height in centimetres and weight in kilograms are the character's height_cm and weight_kg as commonly understood physical measurements.

cases.question: I'm profiling publisher rosters and now want to look at the physical build of George Lucas's heroes. What is the average height of the heroes he created, in centimetres, and their average weight, in kilograms? Please round each average to one decimal place, and only include heroes whose height (for the height average) or weight (for the weight average) is actually known.

I'd like to know how tall the heroes are who share at least one superpower with 3-D Man. Can you give me the average height in centimetres of those heroes, rounded to one decimal place? Please leave 3-D Man himself out of it, and don't count heroes whose height isn't known.

I'm writing an article about green-skinned flying villains and need a body-statistics fact. What is the average weight, in kilograms, of all green-skinned villains who can fly? By villain I mean a character whose moral affiliation is Bad. Please include only characters whose weight was actually measured-any character whose weight was never measured should be left out of the average. Give me just the single number, rounded to the nearest kilogram.
cases.evidence: Flight: the power to fly.

cases.question: I'm picking powers for a lightweight male hero archetype. How many different superpowers are held by at least one male superhero who weighs under 70 kilograms? Heroes whose weight isn't recorded shouldn't count as weighing under 70.

I'm putting together a trivia fact box on tiny heroes. Could you tell me the hair colour of the shortest human superhero? Please treat heroes with no recorded height as unmeasured rather than as being the shortest. I just need the colour, nothing else.

I want to know about the lightest superhero whose weight has actually been recorded. Among all heroes sharing that lightest weight, give me the largest number of superpowers any of them has. If such a hero has no powers, that counts as 0. Please return just that one number.
cases.evidence: A superpower is one power a hero has, identified by its name.

cases.question: I'm auditing identity info on our hero profile pages. How many neutral-alignment heroes have a known full name? Just give me the count.
cases.evidence: By "full name" I mean the hero's real-world identity name, not the superhero/costume name.

cases.question: I'm building a profile page crediting the fastest characters. Among all superheroes that share the top Speed attribute value (everyone tied at the highest Speed value counts), can you list the ones whose real name is known? For each, I need the superhero name and the full name — the civilian identity behind the mask — and nothing else. Please leave out anyone whose real name isn't identifiable.

I'm looking at how designers pair hair and eye colours. For every eye colour that appears on at least one brown-haired hero, how many heroes have that eye colour while their hair is NOT brown? Just give me each eye colour and that count, listing the eye colour with the highest count first. If two eye colours have the same count, the one whose name comes first alphabetically should come first.
cases.evidence: By a brown-haired hero I mean a hero whose hair colour is Brown.

cases.question: I'm comparing the builds of heroes whose power sets overlap with 3-D Man's. What is the average weight in kg of the heroes other than 3-D Man that share at least one superpower with him? Please round it to two decimal places, leave out any heroes whose weight isn't recorded, and return just that single number.
Among distinct patients with at least one uric-acid result above the sex-specific upper limit, what is the ratio of male to female patients?
cases.evidence: For this task, the uric-acid upper limit is 8.0 for males and 6.5 for females.

cases.question: Across laboratory records with PLT > 400 for female patients whose patient profile lists an SLE diagnosis, what is the average ALB value rounded to four decimal places?
List patient IDs, sex, and completed age on 2026-10-09 for patients with at least one laboratory record showing glucose at least 180 and total cholesterol below 250.
List the IDs and completed ages on 2026-10-09 of patients with at least two laboratory results having hematocrit of 52 or higher.
How many distinct patients have at least one positive CRP laboratory result and no recorded patient description?
cases.evidence: Plus-marked CRP results indicate positivity.

cases.question: Among patients in the thrombosis registry born between 1930 and 1940 inclusive who had laboratory tests, what percentage were inpatients? Please give me just the percentage rounded to two decimal places.
cases.evidence: An inpatient is a patient who was admitted to the hospital; an outpatient is a patient who was followed at the outpatient clinic.

cases.question: Among the lab tests with the strongest anti-ribonuclear protein result (i.e., the highest result value), find the highest total bilirubin level and give me that test's total bilirubin level, the date of the lab test, the patient's ID, sex, and birthday. If several of those tests share the highest total bilirubin level, list each of them, one row per test.
cases.evidence: Anti-ribonuclear protein refers to the anti-RNP antibody lab test; total bilirubin refers to the total serum bilirubin lab test (a liver marker).

cases.question: I'm describing our young-patient group and want to show how unusual a raised RNP antibody is in these patients. Could you tell me how many patients in the thrombosis cohort born after 1 January 1960 never had a raised RNP antibody result? A few points: the group should cover every patient born after that date, including patients with no laboratory results at all - they count as never having had a raised result. "Raised" means a result strictly above 10, so a result of exactly 10 doesn't count, and a result of "negative" (no antibody detected) is never raised. Please return just one row with a single integer: the number of these patients.
cases.evidence: RNP: anti-ribonuclear protein antibody; a result of "negative" means no antibody was detected. A raised RNP result is a laboratory result strictly above 10.

cases.question: I'm studying antibody and platelet profiles in mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD). Can you tell me how many patients diagnosed with MCTD alone - meaning MCTD is their only recorded diagnosis - have had at least one platelet reading within the normal range and at least one anti-RNP antibody level above 5 (strictly greater than 5)? I just need the patient count.
cases.evidence: A platelet level within the normal range means from 100 to 400, both ends included; below 100 or above 400 is outside the normal range.

cases.question: As part of the data-completeness review, I'd like to know how much laboratory follow-up our never-examined patients actually have, split by sex. Could you give me, for each sex (F and M), the average number of laboratory test dates recorded for the patients of that sex who have no examination record at all? Please cover the whole registry, all years, and round the averages to two decimal places. Nothing else needed beyond the two averages.
cases.evidence: F denotes a female patient and M denotes a male patient. A laboratory test date is a date on which laboratory tests were recorded for a patient.

cases.question: I'm reviewing autoimmune antibody profiles in our thrombosis registry. Among the female patients who were admitted to the hospital as inpatients, I need to find the laboratory test record with the highest anti-DNA antibody level, for a case review. Please give me the patient ID, the laboratory test date of that record, and the anti-DNA antibody level reported in it - nothing else. Order the results by patient ID, and if several lab test records share the highest level, list each of them.
cases.evidence: Anti-DNA antibody level means the anti-DNA test result recorded in the laboratory tests.

cases.question: Among patients who have ever had an anti-ribonuclear protein (anti-RNP) antibody result above 16 on any laboratory reading, whenever it was taken, how many were admitted to the hospital and how many were followed at the outpatient clinic? Please give one row per care setting, using '+' for admitted to the hospital and '-' for followed at the outpatient clinic, showing the number of such patients in each setting.
For the patients followed at our thrombosis unit's outpatient clinic, what is the highest anti-ribonuclear protein value on record? I just need that single highest value for my review.
cases.evidence: Anti-ribonuclear protein (anti-RNP) is a blood antibody test result recorded for patients.

cases.question: I'm writing a report section on abnormal total protein in female SLE patients and need one summary figure. Among the laboratory records of female patients diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus at an examination visit, where total protein is above the normal bound of 8.5, what is the average deviation of total protein from that bound across all qualifying records, rounded to three decimal places? A few points: an examination visit counts as an SLE diagnosis when systemic lupus erythematosus is among the diseases that visit's diagnosis lists, whether it's the only one or appears alongside others; the normal bound is 8.5, and a record counts as above the bound only when its TP is greater than 8.5; a record's deviation is its TP minus 8.5; and the average should cover all qualifying laboratory records across all dates.
cases.evidence: SLE: systemic lupus erythematosus.

cases.question: What percentage of patients in the registry with a diagnosis of psoriatic arthritis were born in 1960 or later? Please give a single percentage rounded to one decimal place.
cases.evidence: Psoriatic arthritis is a rheumatologic diagnosis recorded for patients in the registry.

cases.question: I'm putting together a demographic summary of our low-albumin patients. Could you tell me how many patients with an albumin measurement below 3.5 are female and how many are male? I'd like one row per sex group showing the sex (F or M) and the number of patients in that group.
cases.evidence: F stands for female and M stands for male.

cases.question: I'm preparing a department audit on how often anti-ribonuclear protein testing comes back clearly elevated among the women in the thrombosis cohort. Among the women in the cohort, what percentage of those with an available anti-ribonuclear protein test result had a clearly elevated result? Please give me the percentage rounded to two decimal places on the 0-100 scale. Note: elevated means a titer strictly above 1:64. Patients never tested for anti-ribonuclear protein should be excluded from both the numerator and the denominator, while a negative reading counts as an available result and is never elevated.
cases.evidence: Anti-ribonuclear protein is a serology test reported as a titer reading; a negative reading is a result of zero titer.

cases.question: What was the average age of the register's patients in 1999, considering all patients who ever had marked or worse proteinuria on a lab test? Age in 1999 means 1999 minus the patient's year of birth. Marked or worse proteinuria means grade 3 or 4 on the original scale, or 300, 1000 or above on the scale used since 1987; traces and grades 1 and 2 don't count. I just need the one average number, in years.
cases.evidence: U-PRO = proteinuria result of a laboratory test; TR = traces of proteinuria.

cases.question: I'm looking at patients whose anti-ribonuclear protein antibody measurement came out higher than 32. Of those patients, how many were women and how many were men? Note that 'higher than 32' means strictly above 32, not equal to it, and a patient qualifies if any of their laboratory measurements exceeded 32.
cases.evidence: A woman means a patient recorded as F, and a man means a patient recorded as M.

cases.question: I'm studying how early in life a patient in the thrombosis cohort can show a high anti-ribonuclear protein (RNP) reading. Please tell me the youngest age, in whole years, at which a patient had a laboratory test showing an anti-RNP result of at least 64. Age in whole years means the year of the test minus the year of birth. If several patients or tests share that youngest age, report that age once. I just need that single youngest age value, nothing else.
cases.evidence: Anti-ribonuclear protein (RNP): an antibody measured in the laboratory panel, reported as a titer number or as negative.

cases.question: For the patients in the registry with a diagnosis of psoriatic arthritis, I'd like to know: (1) the total number of laboratory tests recorded for these patients, counting tests from all dates, and (2) how many of these patients have no laboratory tests recorded at all (i.e., patients with no laboratory record count as having no laboratory tests).
cases.evidence: Psoriatic arthritis: a rheumatic disease diagnosis.

cases.question: For our annual report, I need the count of patients in the thrombosis cohort who showed thrombosis at any examination performed between 01/01/1997 and 12/31/1997, inclusive. Please give me just that number of patients.
cases.evidence: Thrombosis refers to the formation of blood clots, recorded at each examination as a graded finding.

cases.question: I'm putting together a monitoring checklist for SLE patients. Among the thrombotic episodes recorded for patients diagnosed with SLE, which single symptom appears most frequently? I just need the symptom name back. Please count all recorded episodes with no date restriction. If two symptoms are equally frequent, give the one that comes first alphabetically. Note that a patient counts as having SLE only if their own diagnosis record names SLE among their diseases.
cases.evidence: SLE: systemic lupus erythematosus, an autoimmune disease. Thrombotic episode: an episode in which the patient experienced thrombosis.

cases.question: In our autoimmune disease cohort, what percentage of thrombosis patients were diagnosed with SLE at the examination visit? I need the percentage on a 0-100 scale, rounded to two decimal places. Please use the diagnosis recorded at the examination visit, not the diagnosis on the patient's overall file. This is for a write-up on which diagnoses accompany thrombotic events in this cohort.
cases.evidence: SLE: systemic lupus erythematosus, an autoimmune disease; thrombosis: formation of a blood clot within a blood vessel

cases.question: For the thrombosis cohort, I need to describe how long admitted patients typically wait from their first hospital visit until their first examination. Please give me the average delay in days across admitted patients, based on each patient's own first visit and first examination, rounded to the nearest whole number. A patient counts as admitted whenever her admission entry carries a plus sign, regardless of anything else in that entry.

For a demographics summary of our 1994 laboratory cohort: how many female patients and how many male patients had a normal AST glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase (GOT) index on laboratory tests done during the calendar year 1994? Please give me the patient count for each sex (F and M) and nothing else. The calendar year 1994 means laboratory test dates from 1994-01-01 through 1994-12-31.
cases.evidence: AST glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase (GOT) index within normal range means a value below 60.

cases.question: I'm reviewing thrombosis ward patients and need a chart-review list. Can you give me, for every patient who had a single lab visit where the panel showed both an LDH result strictly between 600 and 800 and urine protein of 300 mg/dL or more, the patient ID and their completed age in years as of 2026-10-09? If any one visit's panel shows both findings, that patient qualifies. Please note that a proteinuria result reported as "at least" a level counts at that stated level (e.g., "at least 300" counts as 300 mg/dL or more), and a plain number is in mg/dL. Nothing else needed, just patient ID and completed age.
cases.evidence: Proteinuria result codes: '-' means negative, 'TR' means trace.

cases.question: For the RA patients whose urea nitrogen was within the normal index, how many more women are there than men? Please give me a single integer: the count of women minus the count of men. Women means sex F and men means sex M, and the difference may be negative.
cases.evidence: Within the UN normal index means UN < 30; RA means a Diagnosis of RA.

cases.question: I'm reviewing renal function in the thrombosis cohort and want to compare how often creatinine runs out of the normal range between men and women. For each sex (M and F), please give me: the number of patients of that sex with at least one creatinine result out of the normal range, the total number of patients of that sex, and the share those patients represent of that sex's total as a percentage rounded to one decimal place. Rules: out of the normal range means a creatinine result of 1.5 or higher; the total per sex counts every patient of that sex on file whether or not any lab result exists for them.
cases.evidence: Creatinine out of the normal range: a CRE value of 1.5 or higher. Male is SEX = 'M'; female is SEX = 'F'.

cases.question: In this cohort, I want to compare the most extreme total cholesterol (T-CHO) readings between patients admitted to the hospital and those followed at the outpatient clinic. Please give me, for each of the two groups, the single highest T-CHO reading, along with the admission status ('+' admitted, '-' outpatient) and the patient ID whose reading is the group's highest. List the admitted group's row first, then the outpatient group's. If several patients tie at a group's highest reading, list each of them.
cases.evidence: T-CHO: total cholesterol. '+': the patient was admitted to the hospital. '-': the patient was followed at the outpatient clinic.

cases.question: I'm reviewing the 1991 lab records of the thrombosis cohort, checking whether heavy proteinuria went hand in hand with lower hematocrit that year, as a sign of anemia in kidney involvement. Among the laboratory tests done in 1991 that reported proteinuria of at least 300 mg/dL, what was the average hematocrit value? Please note: proteinuria levels are measured in mg/dL; a proteinuria result reported only as a lower bound that the reading reached or exceeded still counts as being at least that level; a trace result is below 30 mg/dL; and tests without a hematocrit reading should be left out of the average.

I'm putting together a care-setting summary of severe SLE cases for the rheumatology department. Among patients diagnosed with SLE, considering only those whose only diagnosis is SLE and who had abnormally high proteinuria, how many were admitted to the hospital and how many were followed at the outpatient clinic? Please count each patient based on their full history at the hospital.
cases.evidence: Abnormally high proteinuria means a proteinuria level of 30 or higher.

cases.question: How many patients in our thrombosis ward are followed at the outpatient clinic (rather than admitted) with a normal Rheumatoid Factor and no positive measure of degree of coagulation? Please give me a single number. For context: a normal Rheumatoid Factor is '-' or '+-', a positive measure of degree of coagulation is '+' on any of the coagulation measures (KCT, RVVT, LAC), and an outpatient-clinic patient is one with Admission = '-'. If a patient has no recorded coagulation measure, count them as having no positive measure.

I'm reviewing our cohort and need to identify patients whose most recent laboratory sample on file was collected after 1 January 1997 (strictly later than that date) and whose most recent anti-Scl-70 result on file was normal. Please return only the patient IDs for these patients.
cases.evidence: anti-Scl-70: anti-topoisomerase I antibody, an autoantibody measured in the laboratory. A normal anti-Scl-70 result is a result of 'negative' or 0.

cases.question: For a study of laboratory test patterns, I need to size a cohort. How many female patients have at least one anti-DNA antibody level below 8 (the upper bound of the normal range)? Any laboratory visit of the patient qualifies; there is no time scope. I just need that single count back.
cases.evidence: anti-DNA level: the anti-DNA antibody concentration measured in the laboratory tests

cases.question: For patients admitted to the hospital, how many never had an alkaliphosphatase level above the normal ceiling in their lab results? I just need that single count.
cases.evidence: A patient is admitted when their status is anything other than the outpatient-clinic code; the outpatient-clinic code is '-' and admitted is '+'. A normal alkaliphosphatase level is below 300; a level of 300 or more is above the normal ceiling.

cases.question: Among patients in the thrombosis prediction database whose creatinine level is normal (below 1.5), what is the highest anti-RNP antibody level recorded? Please return just that single number; if several measurements tie for the highest, the tied value is the answer.
cases.evidence: Anti-RNP antibody = anti-ribonuclear protein antibody, measured by the laboratory panel.

cases.question: I'd like to see how severe anemia is distributed across the sexes in the registry. Please give me, for each sex, the number of patients of that sex who ever showed severe anemia on any lab test, with the rows labeled 'female' and 'male'.
cases.evidence: Severe anemia means a hemoglobin value below 7.0 g/dL on a lab test.

cases.question: Among the laboratory tests whose AST glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase (GOT) index was above the normal range (60 or higher), I want to find the test with the highest anti-ribonuclear protein reading. Please give me the patient's identification, the date of the laboratory test, and the anti-ribonuclear protein reading for that test. If several tests tie for the highest anti-ribonuclear protein reading, list every one of them. The date should be the date the laboratory test was performed.
cases.evidence: AST glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase (GOT) index: a liver enzyme measurement; values of 60 or higher are considered above the normal range.

cases.question: In the thrombosis and autoimmune-disease cohort, I want to compare how often lactate dehydrogenase stays in the normal range between patients admitted to the hospital and patients followed at the outpatient clinic. Please give me one row per patient group showing the number of lactate dehydrogenase measurements within the normal range recorded for that group, with the admitted group's row first. Label the rows 'admitted to the hospital' for the Admission = '+' group and 'followed at the outpatient clinic' for the Admission = '-' group. Every laboratory measurement recorded for those patients across the whole study period counts. Nothing else is needed.
cases.evidence: The normal range for lactate dehydrogenase means a value below 500.

cases.question: For patients whose sex is not recorded in the registry, I need two counts for the annual quality report: how many have at least one laboratory result on file, and of those, how many have at least one laboratory result showing elevated total bilirubin. The report covers all dates.
cases.evidence: A patient's sex is not recorded when the registry holds no sex entry for that patient. Total bilirubin of 2.0 or higher counts as elevated.

cases.question: For an audit, I need the number of admitted female patients born between 1945 and 1989 (inclusive) who have an ANA examination where the observed pattern is exactly P, with no other pattern alongside it. Please return just that single count.
cases.evidence: ANA pattern: the pattern observed in the ANA examination, e.g. 'P' or 'P,S'; the admission mark starting with a plus indicates the patient was admitted.

cases.question: I'm screening outpatient clinic patients with anemia for rheumatologic autoimmunity. Among patients who were followed as outpatients (rather than admitted to the hospital) and who ever had a hemoglobin value below 10 on any lab test, who showed the strongest anti-ribonuclear protein antibody response? Please return, for every patient whose anti-ribonuclear protein antibody level reached the highest point ever recorded on their lab tests (list all of them if several share that highest level): the patient ID, the patient's sex, and that highest-ever recorded anti-ribonuclear protein antibody level. Nothing else.
cases.evidence: Anti-ribonuclear protein refers to the antibody measured in the laboratory tests (anti-RNP).

cases.question: Among the patients in the thrombosis prediction data, how many have a first laboratory record showing both a normal glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase (GOT) level and an elevated anti-ribonuclear protein (RNP) concentration? By normal GOT I mean a value below 60, and by elevated RNP I mean a value above 10. By first laboratory record I mean the one with the earliest laboratory test date for that patient. I need just a single count of these patients.
cases.evidence: GOT stands for glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase (also known as aspartate aminotransferase, AST); RNP stands for anti-ribonuclear protein.

cases.question: I'm reviewing the current kidney involvement status of the thrombosis prediction cohort. For every patient who has had a proteinuria test, I need their patient identifier, sex, the date of their most recent proteinuria test, and the proteinuria level measured on that test. "Most recent" means the latest proteinuria test by test date.
cases.evidence: A proteinuria test is a test that measures the level of protein in the urine; the proteinuria level is the result value it reports.

cases.question: I'm screening the thrombosis cohort for a follow-up panel. Can you give me the patient ids of outpatients (patients followed at the outpatient clinic rather than admitted) whose creatinine phosphokinase is in the normal range (below 250) but whose anti-ribonuclear protein antibody level is above 4 (strictly greater than 4)? Please note that an anti-ribonuclear protein result reported as negative means no antibody was detected. I just need the patient ids, nothing else.
